Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles left Naples for Calabria on 24 June 1284.

Charles I of Anjou.fact: However, he fell seriously ill before travelling to Foggia on 30 December.

Charles I of Anjou.fact: He made his last will on 6 January 1285, appointing Robert II of Artois regent for his grandson, Charles Martel, who was to rule his realms until Charles of Salerno was released.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He died in the morning of 7 _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He made his last will on 6 January 1285, appointing Robert II of Artois regent for his grandson, Charles Martel, who was to rule his realms until Charles of Salerno was released. He died in the morning of 7 January.

Charles I of Anjou.fact: He was buried in a marble sepulchre in Naples, but his heart was placed at the Couvent Saint-Jacques in Paris.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.fact: His corpse was moved to a chapel of the newly built Naples Cathedral in 1296.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His first wife, _____ of Provence, gave birth to at least six children
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His first wife, Beatrice of Provence, gave birth to at least six children. Blanche, the eldest daughter of Charles and Beatrice, became the wife of Robert of Béthune in 1265, but she died four years later.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: According to contemporaneous gossips, she persuaded Charles to claim the _____ of Sicily, because she wanted to wear a crown like her sisters
Charles I of Anjou.fact: According to contemporaneous gossips, she persuaded Charles to claim the Kingdom of Sicily, because she wanted to wear a crown like her sisters.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Before she died in July _____, she had willed the usufruct of Provence to Charles
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Before she died in July 1267, she had willed the usufruct of Provence to Charles.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Blanche, the eldest daughter of Charles and Beatrice, became the wife of Robert of Béthune in _____, but she died four years later
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Blanche, the eldest daughter of Charles and Beatrice, became the wife of Robert of Béthune in 1265, but she died four years later.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Beatrice, her younger sister, married Philip, the titular Latin emperor, in _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Beatrice, her younger sister, married Philip, the titular Latin emperor, in 1273.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles II, Charles's eldest son and namesake was granted the Principality of Salerno in _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles II, Charles's eldest son and namesake was granted the Principality of Salerno in 1272.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles the Lame (as he was called) and his wife, Maria of _____, had fourteen children, which secured the survival of the Capetian House of Anjou
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles the Lame (as he was called) and his wife, Maria of Hungary, had fourteen children, which secured the survival of the Capetian House of Anjou. Elisabeth, Charles's youngest daughter, was given in marriage to the future Ladislaus IV of Hungary in 1269, but Ladislaus preferred his mistresses to her.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Elisabeth, Charles's youngest daughter, was given in marriage to the future Ladislaus IV of Hungary in 1269, but Ladislaus preferred his mistresses to her.

Charles I of Anjou.fact: The widowed Charles first proposed himself to Margaret of Hungary. However, Margaret, who had been brought up in a Dominican nunnery, did not want to marry.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: However, _____, who had been brought up in a Dominican nunnery, did not want to marry
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The widowed Charles first proposed himself to Margaret of Hungary. However, Margaret, who had been brought up in a Dominican nunnery, did not want to marry.

Charles I of Anjou.fact: The widowed Charles first proposed himself to Margaret of Hungary. However, Margaret, who had been brought up in a Dominican nunnery, did not want to marry.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The former described Charles as a tyrant to justify the Sicilian Vespers, the latter argued for the cancellation of the crusade against Aragon in _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The former described Charles as a tyrant to justify the Sicilian Vespers, the latter argued for the cancellation of the crusade against Aragon in 1285.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles had continued his imperial predecessors' policies in several fields, including coinage, taxation, and the employment of unpopular officials from _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles had continued his imperial predecessors' policies in several fields, including coinage, taxation, and the employment of unpopular officials from Amalfi.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Nevertheless, the monarchy underwent a "_____" or "Provençalistion" during his reign
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Nevertheless, the monarchy underwent a "Frenchification" or "Provençalistion" during his reign.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He donated estates in the kingdom to about 700 noblemen from France or _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He donated estates in the kingdom to about 700 noblemen from France or Provence.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Around _____, the Florentine historian, Giovanni Villani, stated that Charles had been the most powerful Christian monarch in the late 1270s
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Around 1310, the Florentine historian, Giovanni Villani, stated that Charles had been the most powerful Christian monarch in the late 1270s.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The historian _____ concludes that Charles's dominion "was too large to control"
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The historian Hiroshi Takayama concludes that Charles's dominion "was too large to control".

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Although his empire collapsed before his death, his son retained southern Italy and _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His highest-ranking officials were transferred from their homelands to represent him in other territories: his senechals in Provence were from Anjou; French and Provençal noblemen held the highest offices in the Regno; and he chose his vicars in Rome from among southern Italian and Provençal nobles. Although his empire collapsed before his death, his son retained southern Italy and Provence.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His renowned justiciar, _____ de Caramanico, developed a new political theory
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His renowned justiciar, Marino de Caramanico, developed a new political theory.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Traditional interpretators of Roman law were convinced that the _____ had a monopoly on law-making
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Traditional interpretators of Roman law were convinced that the Holy Roman Emperors had a monopoly on law-making.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In contrast with them, _____ stated that an emperor could not claim sovereignty over a king and emphasised Charles' full competence to issue decrees
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His renowned justiciar, Marino de Caramanico, developed a new political theory. In contrast with them, Caramanico stated that an emperor could not claim sovereignty over a king and emphasised Charles' full competence to issue decrees.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: To promote legal education Charles paid high salaries—20–50 ounces of gold in a year—to masters of law at the _____ of Naples
Charles I of Anjou.fact: To promote legal education Charles paid high salaries—20–50 ounces of gold in a year—to masters of law at the University of Naples. Masters of medicine received similar remunerations, and the university became a principal centre of medical science.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles's personal interest in medicine grew during his life and he borrowed _____ medical texts from the rulers of Tunis to have them translated
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's personal interest in medicine grew during his life and he borrowed Arabic medical texts from the rulers of Tunis to have them translated. He employed at least one Jewish scholar, Moses of Palermo, who could translate texts from Arabic to Latin.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He employed at least one _____ scholar, Moses of Palermo, who could translate texts from Arabic to Latin
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He employed at least one Jewish scholar, Moses of Palermo, who could translate texts from Arabic to Latin.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Muhammad ibn _____ al-Razi's medical encyclopaedia, known as Kitab al-Hawi, was one of the books translated at Charles's order
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi's medical encyclopaedia, called Kitab al-Hawi, was one of the books translated at Charles's order.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles was also a poet, which distinguished him from his _____ relatives
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles was also a poet, which distinguished him from his Capetian relatives.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He composed love songs and a jeu-parti (the latter with Pierre d'_____)
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He composed love songs and a jeu-parti (the latter with Pierre d'Angicourt).

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In _____, he wrote a single Occitan cobla (stanza) in an exchange with the troubadour Sordello
Charles I of Anjou.fact: In 1269, he wrote a single Occitan cobla (stanza) in an exchange with the troubadour Sordello.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Bertran d'_____ wrote a poem against the salt tax and Raimon de Tors de Marseilha rebuked Charles for invading the Regno
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Bertran d'Alamanon wrote a poem against the salt tax and Raimon de Tors de Marseilha rebuked Charles for invading the Regno.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The trouvère Adam de la Halle dedicated an unfinished epic poem, entitled _____ of Sicily, to Charles and Jean de Meun glorified his victories in the Romance of the Rose
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The trouvère Adam de la Halle dedicated an unfinished epic poem, entitled The King of Sicily, to Charles and Jean de Meun glorified his victories in the Romance of the Rose.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Dante described Charles—"who bears a manly nose"—singing peacefully together with his one-time rival, Peter III of Aragon, in _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Dante described Charles—"who bears a manly nose"—singing peacefully together with his one-time rival, Peter III of Aragon, in Purgatory.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He designed a tower in _____, but it soon collapsed
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He designed a tower in Brindisi, but it soon collapsed.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He ordered the erection of the _____ in Naples, of which only the palatine chapel survives from his work
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He ordered the erection of the Castel Nuovo in Naples, of which only the palatine chapel survives from his work.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He is also credited with the introduction of _____-style stained glass windows in southern Italy
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He is also credited with the introduction of French-style stained glass windows in southern Italy.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Emperor Frederick II, who was also the ruler of _____, died in 1250
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Emperor Frederick II, who was also the ruler of Sicily, died in 1250. The Kingdom of Sicily, also called the Regno, included the island of Sicily and southern Italy nearly as far as Rome.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: After Charles informed the _____ on 30 October 1253 that he would not accept the Regno, the Pope offered it to Edmund of Lancaster
Charles I of Anjou.fact: After Charles informed the Holy See on 30 October 1253 that he would not accept the Regno, the Pope offered it to Edmund of Lancaster.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Ignoring Louis IX's 1246 ruling that _____ should pass to John, she promised the county to Charles
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Margaret II, Countess of Flanders and Hainaut, had come into conflict with her son by her first marriage, John of Avesnes. Ignoring Louis IX's 1246 ruling that Hainaut should pass to John, she promised the county to Charles.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles's troops ousted the _____ from Florence in April 1267
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Victories by the Ghibellines, the imperial family's supporters, forced the Pope to ask Charles to send his troops to Tuscany. Charles's troops ousted the Ghibellines from Florence in April 1267.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Pope Clement urged Charles to return to the Regno, but he continued his campaign in _____ until March 1268, when he met with the Pope
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Pope Clement urged Charles to return to the Regno, but he continued his campaign in Tuscany until March 1268, when he met with the Pope. In April, the Pope made Charles imperial vicar of Tuscany "during the vacancy of the empire", a move of dubious legality.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: After L'_____'s subsequent victory at Sciacca, only Capece resisted, but he also had to surrender in early 1270
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles made William l'Estandart the commander of the army in Sicily in August 1269. L'Estandart captured Agrigento, forcing Frederick of Castile and Frederick Lancia to seek refuge in Tunis.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles concluded an agreement with the _____ chiefs, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties in February 1272
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's troops took possession of the town with the assistance of the leaders of the nearby Albanian communities. Charles concluded an agreement with the Albanian chiefs, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties in February 1272.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In November 1272 Charles commanded his officials to take prisoner all _____ within his territories, except for the Guelphs, and to seize their property
Charles I of Anjou.fact: In November 1272 Charles commanded his officials to take prisoner all Genoese within his territories, except for the Guelphs, and to seize their property. Pope Gregory condemned his aggressive policy, but proposed that the Genoese should elect Guelph officials.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Ignoring the Pope's proposal, the _____ made alliance with Alfonso X of Castile, William VII of Montferrat and the Ghibelline towns of Lombardy in October 1273
Charles I of Anjou.fact: In November 1272 Charles commanded his officials to take prisoner all Genoese within his territories, except for the Guelphs, and to seize their property. Pope Gregory condemned his aggressive policy, but proposed that the Genoese should elect Guelph officials.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Bulgarian ruler, _____, was the first to conclude a treaty with him in 1272 or 1273
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Bulgarian ruler, Konstantin Tih, was the first to conclude a treaty with him in 1272 or 1273.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In the autumn of 1275 the _____ offered to make peace with Charles, but he did not accept their terms
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Convinced that only Rudolf I could achieve a compromise between the Guelphs and Ghibellines, the Pope urged the Lombard towns to send envoys to him. In the autumn of 1275 the Ghibellines offered to make peace with Charles, but he did not accept their terms.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: An agreement about _____'s rule in Arles and his marriage to Rudolf's daughter, Clemence, was signed in May 1280
Charles I of Anjou.fact: To ensure that Charles fully abandoned his ambitions in central Italy the Pope started negotiations with Rudolf about the restoration of the Kingdom of Arles for Charles's grandson, Charles Martel. An agreement about Charles Martel's rule in Arles and his marriage to Rudolf's daughter, Clemence, was signed in May 1280.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: After lengthy negotiations, in the summer of 1279 Rudolf recognised Charles as the lawful ruler of _____ without demanding his oath of fealty
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Margaret of Provence sharply opposed the plan, but Philip III of France did not stand by his mother. After lengthy negotiations, in the summer of 1279 Rudolf recognised Charles as the lawful ruler of Provence without demanding his oath of fealty.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Rumour has it that he visited in disguise _____, Sicily and Viterbo between 1279 and 1280 where he convinced the emperor Michael VIII, the Sicilian barons and Pope Nicholas III to support a revolt
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Rumour has it that he visited in disguise Constantinople, Sicily and Viterbo between 1279 and 1280 where he convinced the emperor Michael VIII, the Sicilian barons and Pope Nicholas III to support a revolt.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Pope Martin declared the war against _____ a crusade and conferred the kingdom upon Philip III of France's son, Charles of Valois, on 2 February 1284
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles met with the Pope in Viterbo on 9 March, but he ignored the Pope's ban on his duel with Peter of Aragon.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He made his last will on 6 _____ 1285, appointing Robert II of Artois regent for his grandson, Charles Martel, who was to rule his realms until Charles of Salerno was released
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He made his last will on 6 January 1285, appointing Robert II of Artois regent for his grandson, Charles Martel, who was to rule his realms until Charles of Salerno was released. He died in the morning of 7 January.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His corpse was moved to a chapel of the newly built _____ in 1296
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His corpse was moved to a chapel of the newly built Naples Cathedral in 1296.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Blanche, the eldest daughter of Charles and _____, became the wife of Robert of Béthune in 1265, but she died four years later
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His first wife, Beatrice of Provence, gave birth to at least six children. Blanche, the eldest daughter of Charles and Beatrice, became the wife of Robert of Béthune in 1265, but she died four years later.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The former described Charles as a tyrant to justify the _____, the latter argued for the cancellation of the crusade against Aragon in 1285
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The former described Charles as a tyrant to justify the Sicilian Vespers, the latter argued for the cancellation of the crusade against Aragon in 1285.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: While withdrawing from _____, they fell into captivity on 6 April 1250
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Robert of Artois died fighting against the Egyptians at Al Mansurah. While withdrawing from Egypt, they fell into captivity on 6 April 1250.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Louis remained in the _____, but Charles returned to France in October 1250
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Louis remained in the Holy Land, but Charles returned to France in October 1250.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Archbishop of Arles and the _____ of Digne ceded their secular rights in the two towns to Charles in 1250
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Archbishop of Arles and the Bishop of Digne ceded their secular rights in the two towns to Charles in 1250.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In November 1255 he ordered Charles to restore _____ to Margaret, but her sons were obliged to swear fealty to Charles
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Ignoring Louis IX's 1246 ruling that Hainaut should pass to John, she promised the county to Charles. He accepted the offer and invaded Hainaut, forcing most local noblemen to swear fealty to him.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The burghers of Cuneo—a town strategically located on the routes from _____ to Lombardy—sought Charles's protection against Asti in July 1259
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles continued to expand his power along the borders of Provence in the next four years. The burghers of Cuneo—a town strategically located on the routes from Provence to Lombardy—sought Charles's protection against Asti in July 1259.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Emperor Frederick II's illegitimate son, _____, had been crowned king of Sicily in 1258
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Emperor Frederick II's illegitimate son, Manfred, had been crowned king of Sicily in 1258. After the English barons had announced that they opposed a war against Manfred, Pope Alexander IV annulled the 1253 grant of Sicily to Edmund of Lancaster.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles met with the _____'s envoy in early 1262
Charles I of Anjou.fact: After the English barons had announced that they opposed a war against Manfred, Pope Alexander IV annulled the 1253 grant of Sicily to Edmund of Lancaster. Alexander's successor, Pope Urban IV, was determined to put an end to the Emperor's rule in Italy.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Worried that further delays might endanger his subjects' loyalty, _____ attacked Charles's army, then in disarray from the crossing of the hills, on 26 February 1266
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He marched towards Naples, but changed his strategy after learning of a muster of Manfred's forces near Capua. Manfred also hurried to the town and reached it before Charles.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: To appease the _____, Charles resigned his senatorship in May 1267
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Pope Clement censured Charles for his methods of state administration, describing him as an arrogant and obstinate monarch. To appease the Pope, Charles resigned his senatorship in May 1267.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles returned to Lucera to personally direct its siege in April 1269.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Saracens and the _____ who had escaped to the town resisted until starvation forced them to surrender in August 1269
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Saracens and the Ghibellines who had escaped to the town resisted until starvation forced them to surrender in August 1269.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles made _____ l'Estandart the commander of the army in Sicily in August 1269
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles made William l'Estandart the commander of the army in Sicily in August 1269.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles hurried to Rome to attend the enthronement of _____ X on 27 March 1272
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles hurried to Rome to attend the enthronement of Pope Gregory X on 27 March 1272.

Charles I of Anjou.fact: John I Doukas of Thessaly and Stefan Uroš I, King of Serbia, joined the coalition in 1273.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Bulgarian ruler, Konstantin Tih, was the first to conclude a treaty with him in 1272 or 1273. John I Doukas of Thessaly and Stefan Uroš I, King of Serbia, joined the coalition in 1273.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: On 3 July 1281 Charles and his son-in-law, Philip of _____, the titular Latin emperor, made an alliance with Venice "for the restoration of the Roman Empire"
Charles I of Anjou.fact: On 3 July 1281 Charles and his son-in-law, Philip of Courtenay, the titular Latin emperor, made an alliance with Venice "for the restoration of the Roman Empire".

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Chess.fact: There is no universally accepted way to delineate the three phases of the game; the middlegame is typically considered to have begun after 10–20 moves, and the endgame when only a few pieces remain.  ==== Opening ==== Competitive players typically learn, memorize, and play well-documented sequences of opening moves.  The most common starting moves for White are 1. d4, which usually lead to substantially different types of positions, and Black has multiple viable responses to both.  Sequences of opening moves are referred to as openings and are catalogued in reference works, such as the Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings.  There are thousands of openings, though only a small fraction of them are commonly played; variations of openings may also be given names.  Openings vary widely in character from quiet positional play (for example, the Réti Opening) to sharp aggressive play (like the Latvian Gambit)

Specific plans or strategic themes will often arise from particular groups of openings that result in a specific type of pawn structure.  An example is the minority attack, which is the attack of queenside pawns against an opponent who has more pawns on the queenside.  The study of openings is therefore connected to the preparation of plans that are typical of the resulting middlegames

The leading finishers in these Interzonals would go through the "Candidates" stage, which was initially a tournament, and later a series of knockout matches.
